issue.title: legacy_eat notebook keeps duplicate block IDs ^z-240410-7y and ^z-240410-7z inherited from the zorg-era eat.md

task_type_fields.impact: bob notebooks check reports 2 standing errors, and a link to either anchor resolves ambiguously.
task_type_fields.repro:
Run `bob notebooks check` on the live vault (athena, 2026-11-12). It reports two errors in `legacy_eat.md`:

    73: [notebook_duplicate_block_id/error] duplicate block ID `^z-240410-7y` in this notebook
    93: [notebook_duplicate_block_id/error] duplicate block ID `^z-240410-7z` in this notebook

Proposed by bob-cli-k3.1, note #1 (the vault-cleanup phase of epic bob-cli-k3). That phase de-zorged `eat.md` into the `legacy_eat` notebook under `body`. The duplicates were already in the zorg-era `eat.md` history, and the migration preserved both historical restaurant rows on purpose. The epic did not introduce them. Fixing them needs Bryan's mapping: decide which row keeps each anchor, re-ID the other, and rewrite any inbound `[[legacy_eat#^z-240410-7y]]` / `-7z` links to the row they actually meant.

issue.creation_reason: bob-cli-k3.1 preserved two historical duplicate eat anchors as directed when moving eat history into legacy_eat; bob notebooks check still reports them as errors and they need Bryan's mapping to resolve.
